Subject: Increased tail-latency during trial — renewal implications

Hi Jonas,

Quick note from CloudFin: over the past three weeks we've observed intermittent P99 latency spikes (~1.8s) on the 'generate' route that correlate with peak usage windows. These events have caused a small number of real-time transaction delays in our customer flows and prompted an internal risk review ahead of our renewal.

We appreciate the team's responsiveness on the tickets, and Laura's team has been helpful, but given the timing of our contract renewal we're evaluating two things: 1) whether we can secure an uptime/latency commitment that covers our peak tail, and 2) whether Redwood will make a one-time commercial concession (credit or discount) for the impact during onboarding.

I attached an export of recent traces and a short impact summary. Can we set expectations for a path forward? We are targeting a renewal decision by mid-April.

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Lee
Head of Platform Reliability
CloudFin Solutions

Attachments: service_impact_log.csv, availability_summary_q1.pdf

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 08:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Increased tail-latency during trial — renewal implications

Anna, Jonas — thanks for raising this. We did a quick pass on the CSV and see several origin-level retries coinciding with backend autoscaling windows. Preliminary hypothesis: request bursts are crossing a threshold that results in transient queueing at the router/KV-cache boundary.

What we can offer immediately:
- Short-term: a 30-day activation of our premium routing profile (prioritized scheduling + dedicated GPU lanes during your peak window) to reduce tail latency.
- Commercial: a 10% usage credit for the impacted billing month contingent on the incident window we can mutually agree on.
- Next: a technical review led by Prioym to recommend persistent changes (e.g., prefix caching adjustments, batching thresholds, and a pod sizing recommendation for a Dedicated pilot).

If that sounds reasonable, Jonas/Marissa can draft an amendment for the renewal that includes a defined pilot and the one-time credit. I can also join the technical review.

Laura Bennett
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, Anna Lee <anna@cloudfin.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Technical assessment: tails and mitigation options (logs attached)

Hi all — I completed a deeper pass on the traces Anna sent and pulled server-side telemetry for the windows mentioned. Key findings:
- P95 remains ~120ms; spikes to P99 (~1.6-1.9s) during sustained 30s bursts where request concurrency briefly doubles.
- Root cause appears to be a combination of bursty traffic + ephemeral cache misses that create KV fetch amplification.
- No evidence of model degradation; token throughput is consistent.

Recommended mitigations (short and medium term):
1) Enable prefix/KV warmup for your most common prompts (reduces cache-miss amplification).
2) Apply a soft rate limit + queueing window with prioritized scheduling on the 'generate' route during your peak 5-10 minute windows.
3) If you need strict tail guarantees, onboard a small Dedicated pool sized for peak concurrency (we estimate 4x your current committed baseline for peaks) and enable our low-latency kernel selection profile.

I've attached a short config diff and an amendment draft that outlines a three-month Availability Guard pilot and suggested Dedicated sizing: proposed_amendment_draft.docx. Happy to review the config in a follow-up call.

— Prioym
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed_amendment_draft.docx

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Anna Lee <anna@cloudfin.com>, procurement@cloudfin.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 07 Apr 2026 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Next steps — Availability Guard pilot + commercial concession

Anna — thanks again for the patience while we investigated. Summary and proposed path for renewal: 

1) Immediate pilot: 3-month Availability Guard (premium routing + dedicated lanes during your peak windows). We will size a small Dedicated pool for peak concurrency as Prioym recommended.
2) Commercial concession: one-time 10% credit applied to the March billing period for the confirmed incident windows once we align on timestamps.
3) If the pilot reduces tail behavior to below 800ms P99 in your peak window, we will incorporate the Availability Guard as a sustainable option in the renewal at the published premium tier rate. If not, we will provide a defined remediation plan and an additional 30-day credit as a good-faith remedy.

Action items:
- Anna: confirm the March incident windows you want used for the credit calculation (start/end timestamps).
- Redwood: we'll publish the proposed amendment (DocuSign link below) and provision the pilot within 5 business days of signature.

DocuSign: https://docusign.example/tds/CF-2026-1043-amendment
HubSpot: https://hubspot.example/record/CF-2026-1043

Best regards,
